inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 16 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 16: a host write to 16 is overwritten on the next update. The retained known-working script drives it: table1_KeyDown/table1_KeyUp (script lines 259-309) hand the right flipper key to DE.VBS vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp, which set Controller.Switch(swLRFlip) with swLRFlip = 82 (excerpt vpm-script-library-flippers). In the retained robo_a34 and robo_a30 Switch Test the held right flipper key makes the ROM print RIGHT FLIPPER at switch 16. The physical counterpart is the right cabinet flipper button (180-5048-01).

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Upper Right Button (86)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWURFLIPBUTBIT = 0x20, published at 86 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. core_updateSw copies only the two lower button bits into the matrix and the synthetic outputs; this upper-button bit would join locals.flipMask only if hw.flippers set the matching upper FLIP_SW bit, and FLIP1516 = FLIP_SWNO(15,16) sets FLIP_SW(FLIP_L) only. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. DE.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant is the PinMAME column's upper-right button bit, but core_updateSw does not copy it and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

DE.VBS names this address swULFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged left-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(2) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sULFlipper = 36) unless the table calls NoUpperLeftFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleLFlip as a number other than True. The constant is the PinMAME column's upper-left button bit, but core_updateSw does not copy it and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball rests on the outhole switch 10; output 25 (R01) kicks it into the trough. The manual lists Outhole Kicker Assy. 500-5082-00 and a 23-840 coil; the ROM's Coil Auto names 25 OUTHOLE.
mechanisms.label: Outhole kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Three balls rest on Trough #1-#3. Output 26 (R02, 23-840, which the ROM's Coil Auto names SHOOTER LANE) ejects one into the shooter lane, where switch 14 sees it before the manual plunger launches it. The retained script's cvpmBallStack orders the switches 13, 12, 11 from the eject end; the manual does not draw their order.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough and eject

mechanisms.behavior: A saucer at the upper left holds the ball on switch 28; output 27 (R03, 27-1300) kicks it out. One of three Playfield Eject Assy. 500-5051-02.
mechanisms.label: Upper-left eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: A saucer at the top center holds the ball on switch 29; output 28 (R04, 27-1300, Ball Guide Eject) kicks it out.
mechanisms.label: Top eject saucer

mechanisms.behavior: A saucer at the top right holds the ball on switch 30; output 29 (R05, 27-1300) kicks it out past the Right Eject Ball Guide. The rules award the Scanner value and a ROBOCOP letter per shot (lamps 17-18 and 25-29).
mechanisms.label: Right eject saucer (Scanner)

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the left kicker hole rests on switch 45; output 30 (R06, 23-800) kicks it vertically onto the VUK Left Flip. Feed Ramp (535-5355-00), which returns it to the left flipper.
mechanisms.label: Vertical Up Kicker

mechanisms.behavior: A kickback at the foot of the left outlane. Switch 17 reports the ball in the lane; when lit (lamp 20 Relite Laser Kick, lamp 45 Laser Kick Outlane) the ROM fires output 16 (23-800 through Q5 TIP36C) to return the ball to play.

mechanisms.behavior: One 22-900 dual-winding coil on the solid-state flipper board moves the left flipper. FLIP1516 makes core_updateSw copy the left cabinet button, public 84, into switch 15 and fabricate 47/48.

mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.label: Left turbo bumper

mechanisms.label: Right turbo bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Four fixed standup targets, Green Target 1 (left) to 4 (right), each with its own switch and lamp (4 down to 1). The parts list prints 4 Bank S.U. Tgt. Assy. 515-5211-14; there is no reset coil.
mechanisms.label: Left four-bank green standup targets

mechanisms.behavior: Three fixed standup targets, Yellow Target 1 (left) to 3 (right), each with a switch and lamp 9-11. The parts list prints 3 Bank S.U. Tgt. Assy 500-5103-16; there is no reset coil.
mechanisms.label: Center three-bank yellow standup targets

mechanisms.behavior: Two fixed 10 Point S.U. Switches (500-5069-00), top and bottom. The retained table has no object for either, so their positions are not established.
mechanisms.label: Two 10-point standup switches

mechanisms.behavior: The manual records the trap ball only through switch 23 Right Trap Ball (500-5035-02) and lamps 19 Trap Ball Top and 22 Red Trap Ball; its parts list prints no assembly for it. The retained table builds it as a captive ball (CapBall1) in the right lane below a target that reports switch 23, matching the drawn positions of lamps 22 (low) and 19 (top). The physical construction is not documented by a retained source.
mechanisms.label: Right trap ball

mechanisms.behavior: The player launches the ball with the ball-shooter assembly (500-5019-04); switch 14 reports a ball in the shooter lane. The ROM's 100K top lane award is for a plunge through a flashing ball guide.
mechanisms.label: Manual plunger and shooter lane

mechanisms.behavior: Passive paths: the left and right return lanes, the right outlane, the 2-0-9 top lanes, the Left Catch Ramp and Right Ramp with a ramp switch each (Ramp Sw. Act. Wire 535-5361-00), and the spinning target 515-5236-00 whose Spin. Sw. Actuator Wire (535-5319-00) works switch 44. No motor, diverter or magnet is fitted.
mechanisms.label: Lanes, ramps and spinner
